title: Accuracy of a deployed boarding-risk flag in a hospital patient flow command centre: a diagnostic accuracy study
abstract: Objective: to estimate the sensitivity, specificity and calibration of a vendor boarding-risk flag used by a patient flow command centre. Design: consecutive series of admission decisions from March 2025 to February 2027 with a documented timestamp reference standard (boarding of four hours or more). Results and conclusions will be written after the analysis.
introduction: Command centres flag patients at risk of prolonged boarding, but published validations of such tools show moderate accuracy that falls at night and varies by service, and the local tool has only vendor validation.
methods: Score log linked to emergency timestamps and ward arrival times; reference standard rule fixed in advance and applied blind to the flag; sensitivity and specificity at the deployed threshold with day-level cluster-robust intervals; calibration; comparison with occupancy alone; subgroups by time of day, weekday and service.
results: No data have been analysed yet. The report will present the flow of admission decisions, the two-by-two table, accuracy by subgroup, calibration plots and the occupancy comparison.
discussion: The discussion will interpret the flag's accuracy against published validations, weigh the treatment paradox from escalation, and state what the command centre should change.
limitations: One hospital; escalation bias; timestamp-based reference standard.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will be limited to the flag's accuracy and will not claim that the command centre reduced boarding.
reportingChecklist: TRIPOD, with STARD 2015 items for the binary flag
summary: TRIPOD-structured draft with results left empty until analysis.
